title: Ranges, costs and sensitivity
objective: Name the first assumptions to validate when the ROI range changes widely.
clearance: Rewritten draft; pending SME and partner clearance

blocks.x: A single number invites false confidence. Show a range, include the real costs, and use sensitivity to find what to validate next.

Present **conservative**, **base**, and **upside** scenarios with transparent assumptions. In this module's fictional ROI Lab, the base scenario produces a risk-adjusted annual capacity value of $41,472 against a first-year all-in cost of $30,000. That gives a net first-year modeled value of $11,472 and a net ROI of about 38%. The conservative scenario produces $13,608 of risk-adjusted value, which is below cost. Keep it visible.

items: **Net ROI** = (benefit − cost) ÷ cost, with benefit and cost over the same period.
**Benefit/cost multiple** = benefit ÷ cost. This is not net ROI.

**Simple payback (months)** = cost ÷ (annual benefit ÷ 12). The ROI Lab uses this simplified form, which gives about 8.7 months in the base case. It is not a full cash-flow or NPV model. Say so before comparing it with a multi-year calculator.

blocks.x: Include all the relevant costs: platform, implementation, adoption and enablement, and measurement.
Use sensitivity to decide what to validate
If the range is wide, the assumptions that drive it are where validation effort should go. Sensitivity is not a license to pick the most attractive result.

blocks.label: Boundary
blocks.x: Don't compare an annual benefit with a three-year cost, and don't call a negative-return scenario a success. Preserve the downside result and explain its drivers.

Glean's business-case training recommends presenting multiple ROI scenarios rather than a single number. Showing the conservative case alongside base and upside lets a finance reviewer see how the outcome depends on adoption and recapture, and which assumptions matter most.

blocks.title: Three scenarios (fictional)
blocks.alt: A bar chart of three fictional annual benefit scenarios: conservative at 1.2 million dollars, base at 2.0 million, and upside at 3.1 million. The conservative case is emphasized because it shows whether the decision holds under cautious assumptions.
blocks.caption: Fictional values for illustration only.

practice.x: The modeled ROI ranges from negative to strongly positive across the three scenarios. Name the first assumptions you would validate.

worked.x: Validate the time burden per event, the active population and adoption, the event frequency, and the recapture rate, with a reallocation plan. Then confirm scope, cost, and the quality guardrails.
State clearly whether the modeled benefits are capacity or cash. Keep the downside result in the readout, with an explanation of what would have to be true for each scenario.
